rubrics.criterion: After the fix, no Go-level handle abstraction declared in the core package couples more than one COM capability area: the all-purpose handle declaration produced by the generalization is gone (or has been re-scoped), and every handle abstraction that remains (any new or re-introduced one) covers a single capability area such as identity and lifetime or late binding by member name.
rubrics.rationale: This case's central defect is that the one declared handle type in the core package absorbed identity, late binding, enumeration, and connection advising simultaneously; a solution that leaves any multi-area handle declaration in place has resolved nothing at the level the task is about.

rubrics.criterion: The embedding-root wrapper has no capability bodies beyond identity and lifetime in either of the file variants that implement it per platform: the late-binding, enumeration, and advising method bodies added to it during the generalization are removed from the non-Windows variant of the wrapper's implementation files and from the Windows variant alike.
rubrics.rationale: In this library the root wrapper is embedded by every other wrapper and every capability body is mirrored across a platform-paired file; a repair that trims only the variant visible to the local build leaves inherited obligation relationships intact in the other configuration, which is the unique trap created by this repository's platform-companion convention.

rubrics.criterion: The late-binding wrapper no longer declares element-enumeration methods (the collection-cursor overrides composed from the collection property), and every method it does declare falls within the capability area its own native interface contract provides.
rubrics.rationale: The generalization gave this wrapper collection-cursor methods implemented by re-fetching the collection property each call, so it looked like a collection handle despite its underlying contract containing no collection capability; this is the case's clearest instance of a capability override placed where the native contract cannot honor it, distinct from the propagation through the base wrapper.

rubrics.criterion: Every helper function in the helper package takes its handle parameter as the narrowest sufficient type: the late-binding helpers depend on late binding only (a single-capability abstraction of that area, or the concrete wrapper that natively owns it), the connection-setup helper depends on identity and lifetime only, and none of the helper parameters is, or requires, the previous all-purpose handle type or any renamed equivalent of it.
rubrics.rationale: All nine call-style helpers and the connection helper were re-typed to the all-purpose handle in one sweep while individually using one to three methods of it; the entire consumer-side point of this task is that each helper's parameter communicates exactly the capability surface that helper exercises.

rubrics.criterion: The late-binding helpers reproduce the same observable dispatch behavior as before the generalization for callers passing a concrete late-binding wrapper: method invocation and property get/put/put-by-reference each still resolve the member name to a display ID and invoke it with the same dispatch mode that helper always used, and a call with no arguments behaves as before.
rubrics.rationale: The previous helper bodies delegated to a wrapper-specific one-step convenience carrying a dispatch-mode constant, so any re-typing to a narrower surface must reconstruct exactly those dispatch modes (including the by-reference form, which had no one-step equivalent on the shared surface) or existing programs would silently change what they do to objects.

rubrics.criterion: The collection helper still obtains the enumerator through the collection property that objects publish and consumes it through the concrete enumerator wrapper, and the connection helper still performs its container lookup, connection-point resolution, and sink registration exactly as before, so all of these helpers differ only in the declared type of their handle parameter.
rubrics.rationale: This task is a re-typing, not a re-engineering; these two helpers embody the flows (collection walking and event-sink wiring) a solver is most likely to disturb while touching signatures, and this case deliberately keeps their mechanism stable to make the parameter-surface change the only real difference.

rubrics.criterion: No generalization-era artifacts are left behind as dead code: the all-purpose handle declaration is removed rather than left unreferenced or renamed with the same method set, and no explanatory comments, doc claims, stub bodies, or override methods remain anywhere in the package whose only purpose was to satisfy that handle.
rubrics.rationale: In this instance the generalization planted both a broad declaration and the comment blocks that document it as a completed cleanup; a solution that represents the removal of unused obligations as a change to dependents alone, leaving the umbrella declaration and its motivating comments parked in the package, has not actually removed the dead weight.

rubrics.criterion: The helper package now contains copies of core-package dispatch machinery instead of depending on it narrowly — raw display-ID array resolution, raw variant invocation sequences, or vtable-pointer arithmetic implemented directly in helper-package source, rather than being reached through wrapper methods.
rubrics.rationale: This instance removed the large surface the helpers previously used, and the most tempting shortcut to keep them working, given the low-level functions are internal to the core package, is re-implementing them inside the helper package — a duplication this case specifically does not want created in the name of narrowing.

rubrics.criterion: The helper package's exported API keeps its names, function shapes, and result and error types such that existing caller code that passed the concrete late-binding wrapper compiles without modification and needs no new conversions or extra arguments.
rubrics.rationale: The generalization widened these parameters precisely so concrete-handle callers keep working; a repair that narrows responsibility by breaking existing callers inverts the case's purpose, and the repository consumes these helpers in its own examples and tests, so any such break is directly observable.

rubrics.criterion: The fix alters the concrete-wrapper runtime behavior or failure semantics of pre-existing calls: a dispatch mode different from the original one for some helper (for example, property-write helpers no longer distinguishing property put from property put by reference), a different error value or error classification on any failure path, or an existing exported method of a wrapper whose signature or semantics changed.
rubrics.rationale: Every wrapper in this case is identical pre- and post-episode for pre-existing callers only because of Go's method-shadowing, and the interfaces involved implement error codes with distinct Win32 meanings (not-implemented versus no-such-interface); those are exactly the behavioral edges this repository's users and tests would notice, so any drift here is a defect introduced by the rework itself.

rubrics.criterion: The solution modifies surface unrelated to the handle-abstraction rework: signatures or behavior of the deprecated fluent API, the safe-array and marshaling helpers, the type/runtime metadata wrappers, the callback sink, or the low-level syscall plumbing and interface-ID constants.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's generalization was a well-bounded re-typing, and the surrounding commitment relationship covering which files were left untouched is part of the case's own scope statement; a grader needs to catch the routine failure mode of an agent expanding the refactor into neighboring modules.
